summary: Configured NFS share of /srv/nfs/shared on node1, exported to node2's IP only (rw,sync,root_squash), and mounted it persistently at /mnt/shared on node2 via /etc/fstab. Created matching dataops:dataops (UID/GID 4500) identities on both nodes and set the shared directory to dataops:dataops mode 2770. Verified files created from either node preserve consistent ownership/permissions on the other. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: restarted node1 and node2 sequentially (one at a time), confirmed changed boot_id on each, and verified NFS server/export (node1) and auto-mount/data (node2) fully recovered post-restart with correct ownership and read/write access preserved.
actions_performed: Verified OS (Ubuntu 16.04) and absence of dataops user on both nodes
Created dataops group/user with UID/GID 4500 on node1 and node2
Created /srv/nfs/shared on node1, set owner dataops:dataops mode 2770
apt-get update + installed nfs-kernel-server on node1, nfs-common on node2; resolved a stale dpkg lock on node1
Added export line to /etc/exports on node1 restricted to node2's IP with rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash; ran exportfs -ra and restarted nfs-kernel-server
Created /mnt/shared on node2, added fstab entry, mounted via mount -a -t nfs
Verified cross-node file creation preserves dataops:dataops ownership and 2770 mode; verified root_squash behavior
Captured baseline boot_id/service/export/mount state on both nodes plus a baseline test file

Restarted node1 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified nfs-kernel-server/rpcbind active, export intact, data/ownership preserved, and client (node2) could still read/write
Restarted node2 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified fstab auto-remounted /mnt/shared with correct ownership/mode and read/write access
Cleaned up test files, left share empty
